Question Choices: Find the inverse of the diagonal matrix [[5, 0], [0, 10]]. Enter the second row.
Hints: Invert each diagonal entry.|Off-diagonal entries stay zero.
Solution: When ad-bc is nonzero, [[a,b],[c,d]]^(-1)=(1/(ad-bc))*[[d,-b],[-c,a]]. A diagonal matrix with nonzero diagonal entries is inverted by taking their reciprocals. Check both products against the identity. Inverse=diag(1/5,1/10); second row=(0,1/10).

Question Choices: Select. A system's coefficient matrix has determinant 0. Can it be solved by X = A^(-1)B? ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: A zero determinant means no inverse exists.|Another method is needed.
Solution: For [[a,b],[c,d]], det=ad-bc. A square matrix is invertible exactly when its determinant is nonzero. If the determinant is zero, no inverse exists; a corresponding system may have no solutions or infinitely many, depending on the right-hand side. No — A is not invertible.

Question Choices: Solve AX = B for X when A is the 2x2 identity matrix.
Hints: The identity leaves X unchanged.|IX = X.
Solution: The identity has diagonal ones and other entries zero; the zero matrix has all entries zero. For an m by n matrix A, I_m A=A=A I_n. A compatible product with a zero matrix is a zero matrix of the product's dimensions. X = B.
